generalfeedback: To solve this problem you will need to use the product rule calc_product_rule and the chain rulecalc_chain_rule. Let \(g({{CT:0}})={{CT:2}}\) and \(f({{CT:0}})=g({{CT:0}})^{{CT:3}}\). Then, by the chain rule: \[\frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[{{CT:1}}\right] = \frac{df}{dg}\cdot\frac{dg}{d{{CT:0}}}.\] In order to calculate \(\frac{dg}{d{{CT:0}}}\) you need to use the product rule, by defining two new functions: \(h({{CT:0}})={{CT:0}}\) and \(i({{CT:0}})={{CT:4}}\) so that \(g({{CT:0}})=h({{CT:0}})i({{CT:0}})\). So, \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}[{{CT:2}}] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{dh}{d{{CT:0}}}\cdot i + h\cdot \frac{di}{d{{CT:0}}}\\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle [{{CT:5}}]{{CT:4}} + {{CT:0}}[{{CT:6}}] \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:7}} \end{array}\] Hence, \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[{{CT:1}}\right] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{df}{dg}\cdot\frac{dg}{d{{CT:0}}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:8}} \cdot [{{CT:7}}] \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:9}} \end{array}\]
